title: Material and care constraints reach political life through distinct friction and meaning routes
source_unit: Deliberately non-pooled comparison of CPS voting-friction respondents, SIPP care/work transitions, ATUS diary respondents, ANES panel respondents, and CCES respondents

observations.period: November 2024 election; CPS citizen voting-age population and reported nonvoters

denominator.unit: published percentage base for citizen voting-age population; nonvoter reasons use 18.161 million reported nonvoters as a separate denominator

observations.method: Census CPS Voting and Registration Supplement published estimates; registration, voting, and nonvoter-reason distributions are retained as distinct population endpoints.
observations.uncertainty: Survey estimates can differ from administrative data because of nonresponse, vote misreporting, wording, and administration. Reasons are self-reported and not a mutually exclusive causal model.
observations.subgroup: Citizen voting-age population and reported nonvoters age 18+; schedule, health/access, transport, and candidate/issue routes are separate categories.
observations.counterinterpretation: A schedule conflict is not proof of care or work pressure, illness is not proof of institutional exclusion, and candidate dissatisfaction is not apathy; turnout is not the full political-action universe.

observations.period: 2024; CPS nonvoter barrier conditioning by social position

denominator.unit: published subgroup percentage bases; income, age, race, education, and residence-duration universes differ

low_income_nonvoters_illness_disability.unit: percent among nonvoters in families under $10,000; reported margin of error ±7.1 points

high_income_nonvoters_schedule_conflict.unit: percent among nonvoters in families at $150,000 or more; reported margin of error ±3.6 points

recent_address_registration_problems.unit: percent among citizens at address less than one year; reported margin of error ±2.1 points

observations.method: Published CPS Table 10 and related registration tables; subgroup universes and published margins of error are retained rather than pooled into one gradient.
observations.uncertainty: These are descriptive subgroup estimates with different universes and no reproduced covariance tests. Income and residence-duration sections have restricted definitions and do not identify the sequence of moving, registration, work, health, or care.
observations.subgroup: Age, family-income, and residence-duration subgroups among nonvoters or citizens as defined by the Census tables.
observations.counterinterpretation: The subgroup pattern may reflect composition, identity, survey response, institutional rules, or access conditions; it does not establish that a social position caused the reported barrier.

observations.period: 2024; SIPP child-care work prevention and following hardship within stable SNAP-status pairs

denominator.unit: valid person transition pairs in the stable no-SNAP cell; prevention and hardship outcome cells have separate smaller denominators

stable_snap_care_prevented_work_rent_har.unit: percent in 23-person prevention cell; approximate 95% CI 21.7332-65.5706

stable_snap_care_prevented_work_utility_.unit: percent in 23-person prevention cell; approximate 95% CI 11.3927-53.3971

stable_no_snap_care_prevented_work_utili.unit: percent in 71-person prevention cell; approximate 95% CI 7.5738-26.1516

observations.method: Same-person November-to-December SIPP transition paired with annual fall child-care work-prevention fields and following-month hardship; 240 Fay-BRR replicate weights.
observations.uncertainty: The annual care field is not a dated election or political event, the prevention cells are small, and hardship has separate valid universes. The result does not identify a causal care effect or a later political response.
observations.subgroup: Reference parents in stable SNAP-status person pairs, conditioned on child-care prevention of work or additional work.
observations.counterinterpretation: Household composition, income, eligibility, care need, employment, and unmeasured resources may explain both hardship and work prevention; hardship does not imply nonvoting or distrust.

denominator.unit: 2024 respondents in supported standardized cells; 2025 is a separate annual sample of 5,895

eldercare_difference_minutes_2024.unit: provider minus nonprovider minutes per diary day; SE 7.134

eldercare_difference_minutes_2025.unit: provider minus nonprovider minutes per diary day; SE 6.794

observations.method: ATUS diary aggregation and standardization across age, sex, labor-force status, household-child status, and education cells with replicate-weight uncertainty.
observations.uncertainty: Annual samples are not a panel and provider status is not a dated shock. The time contrast does not measure political availability, turnout, trust, or the cause of the time allocation.
observations.subgroup: Eldercare-roster providers versus nonproviders in supported standardized cells.
observations.counterinterpretation: Less paid work or socializing may reflect selection, schedule choice, health, distance, recipient need, or family support rather than lost political voice or employment.

observations.period: 2024; ANES pre-election to post-election financial worry, trust, and reported vote; CCES post-election material proxies and action

denominator.unit: valid ANES panel observations for trust cross-tab; CCES proxy cells use separate respondent denominators

cces_both_gig_and_student_loan_trust_and.unit: percent; weighted joint share in n=665 proxy cell

cces_reference_trust_and_action.unit: percent; weighted joint share in n=17,954 reference cell

observations.method: Separate official ANES panel and CCES common-post weighted descriptive comparisons; worry, trust, reported vote, material proxies, and civic action are retained as different estimands.
observations.uncertainty: Financial worry is not a dated bill or care event, and CCES proxy cells are cross-sectional. Party identity, prior beliefs, information, selection, panel retention, and complex-design variance limitations remain.
observations.subgroup: ANES financial-worry rows and CCES joint gig-work/student-loan proxy cells.
observations.counterinterpretation: Material concern can coexist with trust and action, while worry/trust/vote patterns can reflect identity and interpretation rather than material pressure causing political behavior.

related_sources.claim: CPS supplies the voting, registration, nonvoter-reason, and subgroup-friction endpoints.
SIPP supplies the same-person care/work and following-hardship stage.
ATUS supplies the standardized care/time allocation stage.
The prior non-pooled bridge supplies ANES/CCES trust and action context.

boundary: This is a non-pooled material-to-political-friction architecture, not a causal political-participation estimate. It shows separate routes through hardship, time/care capacity, reported access barriers, trust, meaning, civic action, and vote. It does not establish that care, cost, work, health, mobility, or institutional experience caused nonvoting, distrust, or a candidate choice. Same-person dated exposure, attribution, institutional response, remedy, and recovery remain open.
